hero.subtitle: Coffee behind stone walls in Nicosia
hero.lede: We're in an old sandstone workshop inside the Venetian walls. Scroll, and we'll take apart the machine behind every cup.
hero.canvasLabel: A walnut-panelled espresso machine. As you scroll, it pulls a shot and pours it over ice.

ritual.heroLede: We're in an old limestone workshop inside Nicosia's Venetian walls. Scroll down to follow a cup from the first drop of espresso to the pour over ice.
ritual.originsLede: Behind the cup in the barista's hand are three coffees we're roasting this season.

ready.caption: The brass group head is steady at 93 °C and the walnut portafilter is locked in. First drop soon.

extraction.caption: 18 g of fresh coffee under 9 bar of pressure. A thick, hazelnut-coloured crema forms on top.

craft.caption: 36 g of double ristretto in 28 seconds, carried over to the ice while it's still hot.

pour.caption: A 93 °C shot hits ice at 4 °C. Dark chocolate and orange peel lock in straight away.

pour.title: From 93 °C to 4 °C in one pour.
pour.body: The moment a fresh double ristretto hits the ice, the aroma locks in. What's left in the glass is dark chocolate and citrus.

boiler.title: Copper boiler, PID control
boiler.body: A thick copper boiler holds heat for a long time. The PID controller checks the water many times a second and corrects it, so the first cup and the last come out at the same temperature.

groups.title: E61 brass groups, walnut handles
groups.body: E61 group heads carry water at one temperature from the first drop. The walnut handles were turned one by one by a craftsman here in Nicosia.

pump.title: Rotary vane pump
pump.body: The quiet pump manages pressure in three stages: pre-infusion, peak, decline. Every coffee has its own curve, and some like it gentler.

callouts.outro: The machine is lovely, but people still do the work.

manifesto.p1: Nicosia's yellow stone soaks up the sun all day and is still warm under your hand at dusk. We like coffee the same way: unhurried, with the heat still in it.
manifesto.p2: Stainless steel machines run under 500-year-old arches. On one side, scales, probes and profile curves. On the other, smell and sound. They share a bench.

roasts.title: Three origins, three characters.
roasts.lede: Three coffees from this season's lots. Keep scrolling to go through them.

espresso.name: Espresso
espresso.body: Nine bar, eighteen grams, thirty seconds. Red-brown crema, dark chocolate at the end.

pourover.name: Pour-Over
pourover.body: Slow pours through a V60 or Kalita Wave. Floral, light like tea, and it changes as it cools.

coldbrew.name: Cold Brew
coldbrew.body: Sixteen hours in cold water. The coolest thing you can drink in Nicosia on an August afternoon.

cezve.name: Cypriot Coffee
cezve.body: Brewed in a copper cezve on hot sand, with the foam skimmed off carefully. The oldest recipe we have.

cta.title: We roast on Thursdays. You can smell it from the end of the Arasta.

beans.title: The coffees we roast
beans.lede: We know which farm every coffee comes from. Filter by origin, altitude or process, and open a card to look at its roast curve.

menu.title: Our Menu
menu.lede: Carob from the island, pistachio from Antep, fruit and flowers from Ethiopia. The menu is below, and under it a calculator for making the same cups at home.

tips.pourover: Bloom with the first 50 g of water for 40 seconds, then pour slowly in circles from the centre outwards.
tips.espresso: Flow should start around 6–8 seconds. If it starts earlier, grind a notch finer.
tips.coldbrew: Brew it in the fridge, filter through paper, cut 1:1 with water and serve over ice.

team.title: The people behind the cup
team.lede: There are four of us, one roaster and one stone counter. Every morning we ask the same thing: could this cup be a bit better?
team.hint: Hover or tap to meet them

about.title: A blacksmith's workshop, now a roastery
about.lede: A blacksmith's workshop stood in a back street of the Arasta with its door locked for years. The arches were sound, the walls were yellow stone, and swallows nested in the ceiling.

story.p1: When we got the key in the winter of 2019, we found an anvil, a bellows and fifty years of quiet. Stripping the plaster to get back to bare stone took eleven months.
story.p2: The blacksmith's hearth is now where our roaster's flue goes. Same fire; we just work with coffee instead of iron.
story.quote: The walls were built to protect the city. We look after the small things inside it: the first smell of morning, a neighbour's hello, a good cup.

philosophy.title: Small batches, close attention.
philosophy.p1: Every batch on our 12 kg, Loring-style hot-air roaster gets its own profile. The round, syrupy body of our espresso blends comes from the Probat drum roaster.
philosophy.p2: We log every batch, check it with a colour reading and approve it at a blind cupping the next morning. If we don't like a batch, it doesn't get sold.

points.b: Agtron colour reading on every batch
points.c: Sold within a week of roasting

sustain.title: At the same table as the grower.
sustain.p1: We buy most of our coffee directly from producers, with no middlemen, and pay for quality rather than the commodity price. You can trace every sack back to its farm.
sustain.p2: Spent grounds go to two community gardens in Nicosia as compost, and a local workshop sews the jute sacks into bags.

contact.title: A stone doorway inside the walls.
contact.lede: Walk from the Selimiye towards the Arasta. You'll smell the roasting before you see the door.
